title: Backend entry domain http methods
question: Walk through the common HTTP methods and status code ranges you'd use when building a REST API, and what each communicates to the client.
idealAnswer:
Covers the core methods and their intent: GET (read, no body change), POST (create or trigger an action), PUT (replace a resource), PATCH (partial update), DELETE (remove a resource)

Explains the status code ranges: 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content), 3xx redirection, 4xx client error (the request itself is wrong), 5xx server error (the server failed even though the request was valid)

Picks specific codes correctly in context, e.g. 201 Created with a Location header after a successful POST, 204 No Content for a successful DELETE with nothing to return, 400 for malformed input vs 422 for well-formed but semantically invalid input

Distinguishes 401 Unauthorized (not authenticated) from 403 Forbidden (authenticated but not allowed), a very common mix-up

Bonus: mentions that returning the right status code matters for more than style, clients, caches, and monitoring all branch on it programmatically
